sources_considered.why: Reports Jane Street's $6 billion AI cloud commitment to CoreWeave, a large buyer outside the hyperscaler and lab group.
Reports The Information's estimate that OpenAI and Anthropic account for roughly half of the big clouds' combined backlog, which supports the concentration part.
Reuters version of the Jane Street story. Hidden characters make exact quotation unreliable.
Names Jane Street, Hudson River Trading, Cohere and Mistral as customers but gives no dollar amounts for non-lab buyers. Not needed beyond the Jane Street report.
xAI is an unprofitable AI lab funded by non-hyperscaler investors. It is a borderline case for the speaker's category, so it was not used as decisive.

receipt.public_excerpt: CoreWeave announced a $6 billion AI cloud agreement with Jane Street, alongside a $1 billion equity investment, significantly expanding their partnership.

evidence_items.explanation: Jane Street, a trading firm that is neither a hyperscaler nor a subsidized AI lab, committed $6 billion to AI cloud compute. That runs against the claim that only hyperscaler-propped AI labs can pay for even a fraction of the compute.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Two startups account for half the cloud boom', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: Together with OpenAI, Anthropic is responsible for roughly half of the $2 trillion in combined backlog at Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle, the report says.

evidence_items.explanation: Two loss-making labs account for about half of all contracted cloud backlog at the four largest providers. This supports the claim that AI compute demand is heavily concentrated in hyperscaler-backed labs.

unresolved_gaps: No source measures total AI data-center demand from buyers outside hyperscalers and their subsidized labs, so how large the exceptions are in aggregate is unknown.
The other half of the cloud backlog includes non-AI enterprise contracts and Meta. Its AI-specific makeup is not disclosed.
